articles.title: He lives with his parents and loves Jesus. Meet Gen Alpha's new heartthrob.
articles.summary: Malachi Barton opens up about "Coven Academy" and his rise as Disney's latest heartthrob.
articles.body:
Young girls are pledging their allegiance to Malachi Barton.

I saw it with my own eyes at the Descendants/Zombies: Worlds Collide tour last summer: tweens and teens yelling "Malachi!" like their lives depended on it while waving pink American flags with his face on them. That was before he even stepped onstage.

"A couple of those, yeah," Barton tells Yahoo in our latest Generation Now interview, laughing when I mention the flags.

"Honestly, I still don't look at myself as that person," he adds.

But he is. At 19, Barton is Disney's latest heartthrob — like the Jonas Brothers and Zac Efron before him — and the company is banking on him. He's starring in a trifecta of key projects: vampire Victor in the Zombies movies and aspiring musician Fletch in the Camp Rock revival film, both on Disney Channel, and now warlock Jake in the Coven Academy series on Freeform. He's also headlining the next leg of the Descendants/Zombies/Camp Rock: Worlds Collide tour , and surprise-released his first single, "Stay for the Credits."

Malachi mania is not merely a Mouse House push. Variety honored him with its Rising Star Award at the 2026 Power of Young Hollywood event in August.

As his star soars, Barton still lives with his parents, Felicia Barton, an American Idol Season 8 alum, and tour manager Loren Barton. He says praying is his "No. 1 outlet," though he's also into surfing, urbexing (aka urban exploration), his car and watches. He surrounds himself with friends who will tell him to "get off [his] high horse."

The bigger his profile gets, the more his personal life has become part of the conversation too. And with Coven Academy premiering Oct. 1 on Freeform (Disney+ and Hulu the next day), Barton is entering yet another big chapter.

Barton seems intent on keeping one foot in normal life even as the other lands on increasingly bigger stages. Here, he talks about navigating both.

I saw full Malachi mania last summer when I took my daughter to the 'Worlds Collide' tour. I've been at this a long time, but I was stunned by the reaction your presence created. What's it like to be that person to people?

It's very weird and very crazy. I will be scrolling on TikTok and a TikTok Live will pop up and this girl will have a cardboard cutout of me behind her. And I'm like, OK, that's not weird at all, but also really cute [ laughs ].

I'm super grateful, that's all I can really say. I'm so grateful to be in a position where I can have a voice to so many young kids and be able to spread kindness and the light of Jesus in all things. Having that platform is super, super rad. I'm so grateful.

You're close with your family, and your faith is obviously important to you. How do those things keep you grounded?

Those are the two things, 100%. I have the best parents ever. Since I was a little, little dude, I've been in baseball and had outlets and other things outside of the business, because this business is crazy. So much fun [too], but it's also wild and up and down. You've got to have your other outlets. My No. 1 outlet is the man upstairs. Those are my grounding factors, for sure.

What's your living situation these days? Do you still live with your parents?

I do — I live with my parents. I love my parents. I love living with them. I bought my first house a little while ago, so that's been really, really wild. I feel like I'm never home anyway. My living situation is literally all over the place. First, we're in Vancouver [shooting Coven Academy ], next we're in New Zealand [for Zombies 5 ]. It's so cool because I get to travel around and see so many different parts of the world. But, yeah, I live with my parents, and we have my two little dogs, Artex and Ranger, and my car.

A BMW M3 . It's outside right now. It's my baby.

You graduated from high school last year. Did you have a traditional-ish school experience? Your graduation looked pretty normal.

I did online [school]. I went to a public elementary school for second and third grade, and then I did online [learning] for literally as long as I can remember. But I feel like I got the high school experience because all of my friends — my tight group of people — aren't in the business, and they were all in high school. So I was doing my school at home, but then I was going to all the football games, the homecomings, the proms, the formals. The teachers knew my name. I was kind of an honorary member of their school.

Honestly, I give a lot of [credit] to my friends because they've grounded me. If I come fresh off a set, they will check me very, very quickly and be like, "Get off your high horse." That's the best thing. So I got a little bit of high school, and my graduation was completely normal.

You experienced the gossip side of fame this summer. How do you deal with that?

I think it's always going to be there. You can't avoid it at all. People will always have an opinion, and that is how this business is. That's what you're signing up for. But the thing I remind myself is that the only opinion that matters is God's. People will continue to speculate and say certain things, and that's OK. They have freedom of speech. They can say whatever they want to. I just do my own thing: stay in my lane, stay at the beach, stay in my car and vibe out.

Your schedule this year is insane: a show, TV movies and a tour. How do you spend a day when you're off the clock?

I literally surf. I'm always in the ocean, and I love [it] so much. The ocean is the most physically and mentally healing place on the planet. That's what I do on my days off. Also, I'm getting into urbexing, which is exploring abandoned places. That's a new thing.

I went to this abandoned golf course in California. It was really cool. I can't expose the location because then it's not going to be abandoned or underground [ laughs ]. You gotta gatekeep.

Are you ever worried someone is going to come chasing after you? I'd be too nervous.

That's what makes it fun, though. The fact that you're not able to do it makes it so much fun.

You're the tween crush now. Who was your celebrity crush when you were younger?

Oh my goodness. … I have been a Jessica Alba guy for a very, very long time. Through and through. Love you, Jessica. I'm trying to think of my tween crush, though — I was always a big Madelyn Cline guy. I loved Outer Banks . And then Florence Pugh — come on, big shout-out. Come on, y'all know ball. Let's go, Florence Pugh, love you. I love all of them.

What's the last thing you binge-watched?

Coven Academy . We got that encrypted link — [the one that's like] Yo, don't send this to anybody. The FBI shows up to your house if you try and screen-record it . I sat down on my couch and binge-watched it in literally the shortest amount of time you can watch it. I just sat there and banged it out.

Is your email address also a giant watermark across the screen while you watch, like it is for me?

Yes, but honestly, the show is so good I just looked past it the whole time [ laughs ].

What is your go-to late-night snack after a night out? Full order.

Taco Bell — 100%. Taco Bell is banger. My order is the chicken Cantina quesadilla, but that's not in season right now. So the chicken Cantina burrito is what is in season at the moment. And then a Mexican pizza. I feel like that's the vibe. Taco Bell all the way — or, if a Chipotle's open, there we go.

How many tattoos do you have, and what do they mean?

I think I have eight or so. This one right here is [based on] Proverbs 27:21 , which says: "The purity of gold and silver is tested by putting it in the fire, and the purity of the human heart is tested by giving it a little fame." That's a scripture that my grandpa texted me a lot. Then I have "family" in Morse code , matching with my parents. I've got Jesus being taken off the cross on my rib, and then I have a sword on my stomach. My first tattoo was three little crosses on my ankle. I have Joshua 1:9 tattooed on my back. I have my parents' names in a cross on my back, and the coordinates to my favorite surf spot, that's matching with my best friend, on my [back].

Now I just need to get a BMW tattoo somewhere. I'll get it on my lower back. It's gonna be lit.

Does this point in your career feel like something you imagined, or has it surpassed what you pictured?

Honestly, I didn't have any expectations going into this. With anything that I do, I just go in like, all right, what happens, happens. You can't control everything. You can't. The world's going to happen how it's going to happen, and you've just got to be hands-off. That's how you live more peacefully, in my opinion.

So I went hands-off, and it blew the expectations that I didn't have out of the water. I never in a million years would have thought — if I were to tell my 8-year-old self, signing his first Disney contract, that this was going to be the case [11, 12 years] later — I never would have believed it. Mind blown.

articles.title: Festival Breakfast Weekend reúne opções diversas de café da manhã a partir de R$ 39,90 na cidade de SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Breakfast Weekend começa neste sábado (26) e reúne hotéis, cafeterias, padarias e restaurantes com combos e buffets especiais; programação segue até 25 de outubro.
articles.summary: Breakfast Weekend começa neste sábado (26) e reúne hotéis, cafeterias, padarias e restaurantes com combos e buffets especiais; programação segue até 25 de outubro.
articles.body:
Café da Manhã. — Foto: Divulgação/Recanto Cataratas Thermas Resort & Convention.

Ainda não sabe o que fazer neste fim de semana? Uma opção para quem gosta de começar o dia com calma e, de preferência, com uma mesa cheia, é aproveitar a nova edição do Breakfast Weekend , que começa neste sábado (26) em São Paulo .

O festival chega à 10ª edição reunindo hotéis, cafeterias, padarias e restaurantes da capital com menus especiais de café da manhã. A programação vai até 25 de outubro, com opções em formato de combo ou buffet e preços entre R$ 39,90 e R$ 129,90.

A ideia é justamente transformar a primeira refeição do dia em programa: dá para escolher desde uma cafeteria para um café mais rápido até aproveitar o buffet de um hotel sem precisar estar hospedado.

Entre os participantes estão nomes como Hilton Morumbi, Grand Mercure Ibirapuera, InterContinental São Paulo, Novotel Morumbi, Mercure Jardins, Nacional Inn Jaraguá, Canopy by Hilton Jardins, WZ Jardins, INNSiDE by Meliá Iguatemi e Itaim, além de unidades da rede Ibis, Cakess, Sweet & Sugar e Padoca do Jaca.

O festival começou em São Paulo com foco principalmente nos cafés da manhã de hotéis, mas, ao longo das edições, ampliou a lista de participantes e passou a incluir também cafeterias, padarias e restaurantes espalhados pela cidade.

Na prática, é uma chance de conhecer lugares novos ou finalmente experimentar aquele café da manhã de hotel que normalmente passa despercebido por quem mora em São Paulo.

Para quem prefere transformar o café em um programa mais demorado, há opções de buffet. Já quem quer encaixar o passeio antes de seguir para outra atividade pode escolher os estabelecimentos que oferecem combos fechados.

Antes de sair de casa, porém, vale conferir as regras do local escolhido. Horários, cardápios, necessidade de reserva e disponibilidade variam entre os participantes.

📅 Quando? De 26 de setembro a 25 de outubro

📍 Onde? Hotéis, cafeterias, padarias e restaurantes da capital

articles.title: Taylor Swift releases 4 new songs for 'Life of a Showgirl: The Encore.' What do critics say?
articles.summary: Swift's songwriting has been called "captivating" and "shockingly tender," though one critic dismissed the new tracks as "derivative and flat."
articles.body:
Taylor Swift has added a final act to her record-breaking album The Life of a Showgirl .

Almost a year after the album's release, Swift dropped The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore on Friday, featuring four new songs: "Patient Zero," "Cleveland!," "Pink Clouding" and "Babylon."

The new songs extend what was already a historic run for The Life of a Showgirl . The album debuted last October with 4.002 million equivalent album units in the U.S. — the biggest week for an album since modern tracking began in 1991 — and became the first album to occupy all of the top 12 spots on the Billboard Hot 100.

Despite its success, a deluxe edition wasn't part of the plan.

Swift appeared to rule out more songs last year, telling the New Heights podcast, "There are no other songs coming… This is 12. There's not a 13th, there's not other ones coming."

Swifties kept looking for clues anyway. Seven months before The Encore arrived, her "Opalite" video included a poster reading "Patient for the Encore" and four judges holding up zeroes. This week, Swift swapped the Os in her social media bios for zeroes and started a countdown that revealed the title of "Patient Zero."

Despite arriving as an add-on to an album released nearly a year ago, the new tracks are getting plenty of attention in their own right. But are the surprise additions worth the encore?

What are critics saying about 'The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore'?

Music critics have been deeply divided by The Encore .

USA Today 's Melissa Ruggieri said the four new songs "deserve an ovation." Of "Patient Zero" itself, she writes, "Her staccato vocal delivery glides over a smooth groove that is augmented by strings in the background, but it's the bridge — it's always the bridge — that shines."

Variety 's Chris Willman said it was "refreshing to get something fast and easily digestible" from Swift, adding, "three of the four new tracks on The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore prove she has no intention of turning in her Tortured Poets membership card any time soon."

The Globe and Mail 's Aisling Murphy said the new tracks were "markedly better" than the rest of The Life of a Showgirl , adding, "A showgirl knows to save her best tricks for the grand finale."

Much of the praise has focused on Swift's songwriting. Ruggieri said the lyrics on "Babylon," the closing track, were "captivating," while Willman called the writing on "Pink Clouding" "shockingly tender."

Others questioned whether the new material adds much to The Life of a Showgirl . The Telegraph 's Poppie Platt gave The Encore one star, calling the songs "derivative and flat" and arguing that Swift's enormous commercial success means she "no longer has the incentive to take creative risks."

The Independent 's Roisin O'Connor was also unimpressed, arguing that the songwriting feels recycled from Swift's older, better work. In her two-star review, she added, "Where is Swift, artistically, now? Because it sounds like she's flailing."

Slate 's Carl Wilson said the tracks "sound fairly similar" to the ones on The Life of a Showgirl , "and similarly are at best a couple of notches above half-successful." He described "Patient Zero" as "perfectly passable, with lilting cadences you'll hum along with when it's playing and likely forget until it plays again," adding, "Maybe we've gotten all the growth from Swift we'll ever get."

Laura Snapes of The Guardian argued that the new material lacked cohesion, saying: "It's hard to tell what any of this has to do with Showgirl (other than pushing the album back to No 1 until Christmas). Every song sounds as though it could have been appended to a different record."

"Cleveland!" has been the most divisive song on The Encore . Many reviewers believed the love song references Swift's husband, Travis Kelce, with the line "He already took me to Cleveland / And showed me The Heights." Kelce grew up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, and Swift has appeared as a guest on his podcast, New Heights .

Ruggieri called the track the catchiest of the four, but O'Connor felt it contained "some of her worst writing," while Wilson said that the song "sucks," as do "all her big love songs about Travis Kelce so far."

Willman said he couldn't decide whether it would "grow on me or gnaw at me," and Business Insider 's Callie Ahlgrim predicted it would "go down as one of the worst songs in Swift's discography."

Why did Taylor Swift release 'The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore'?

The four songs weren't leftovers from the original album. Swift wrote them after The Life of a Showgirl was released in October 2025, when she traveled to Sweden with longtime collaborators Max Martin and Shellback to celebrate its success.

"Really, we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there, and we did what we do when we feel anything at all: We wrote more songs," Swift said when announcing The Encore .

The musician said the songs were "born out of pure gratitude" for fans' response to the album.

The release comes just days before Swift returns to the MTV Video Music Awards , where the music video for "Patient Zero," starring Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell, will premiere Sunday.

Swift will also receive the inaugural Artist Director Honors award at the ceremony. The new award recognizes music artists whose work behind the camera has pushed creative boundaries and advanced visual storytelling.

The honor will also break Swift's tie with Beyoncé as the most decorated artist in VMAs history. The two entered this year with 30 Moon Person awards apiece; the Artist Director award will bring Swift's total to 31.

articles.title: Madrid amanece llena de puertas verdes pintadas: sólo la periodista Gloria Serra puede desvelar la razón
articles.standfirst: La presentadora de ‘Equipo de Investigación’ es protagonista para anunciar la llegada de una nueva película
articles.summary: La presentadora de ‘Equipo de Investigación’ es protagonista para anunciar la llegada de una nueva película
articles.body: Madrid es una de las ciudades más sorprendentes del mundo entero. En la capital de España no paran de suceder cosas. Pues bien, a lo largo de toda la urbe aparecieron, en la mañana de este viernes, 25 de septiembre, pintadas verdes, en forma de puerta, sobre los muros de los domicilios. Gloria Serra, reconocida periodista de nuestro país y presentadora de ‘Equipo de Investigación’, desveló el motivo por el que la ciudad madrileña amaneció de esta manera. Filmin subió un reel en el que Serra era protagonista para investigar el caso de las puertas verdes en Madrid. La periodista se hizo varias preguntas al respecto: “¿Son simples señales? ¿Una puerta a lo desconocido? ¿O una broma del héroe Merlin?”. Las puertas verdes son las entradas a ‘los backrooms’: “Una dimensión desconocida, fuera de nuestro entendimiento. Nosotros intentamos entrar, pero no lo conseguimos. (…) Hemos encontrado muchas por toda la ciudad, cargadas de misterio”. Del mismo modo, la periodista afirmó que había muchas más en la Plaza Mayor, una zona “cinéfila” y de “cine polaco”. Una viandante que entrevista en la pieza afirma que si te acerca a la puerta “escucharás cine polaco en versión original”. “Una versión de Boyero con más ojos”, apuntó otro. Para finalizar, Gloria Serra logró entrar a través de una de las puertas que accedió a la oficina de Filmin. Tras ello, una persona en el interior dijo lo siguiente: “¡Cogedle y ponedle una peli de Tarkovsky!". Lo que se estrena será ‘Backrooms’, la cinta que ya está disponible en la plataforma desde este viernes, 25 de septiembre. “Un umbral que conecta su salón con el mejor cine”, sentenció la presentadora de ‘Equipo de Investigación’.

articles.title: ‘Princess Diaries’ Star Heather Matarazzo Reveals She May Lose Health Insurance If She Doesn’t Work Again Soon: ‘Lots of Actors’ Are in the ‘Same Boat’
articles.summary: “Princess Diaries” star Heather Matarazzo revealed she may not qualify for health insurance if she doesn’t find work soon. The actress, who starred alongside...
articles.body:
"Princess Diaries" star Heather Matarazzo revealed she may not qualify for health insurance if she doesn't find work soon.

The actress, who starred alongside Anne Hathaway in the "Princess Diaries" films as Lilly Moscovitz, replied to a post from "Atypical" actor Jack Haven that revealed they needed work in order to qualify for health insurance through SAG-AFTRA.

The guild offers a health plan for its members that requires a "minimum earnings" threshold be met to qualify. However, booking projects in the entertainment industry is often unpredictable and fluctuates, which leads to larger gaps between employment opportunities and ultimately makes meeting that threshold more difficult.

"I'm in a bit of an emergency situation," Haven shared in a YouTube video this week. "I need to make $4,000 by the end of the month in order to qualify for SAG health insurance starting in January."

The actor shared their skills and said they will do "pretty much any job," encouraging anyone open to hiring them on a production under SAG to contact them over email.

Matarazzo replied to a post about Haven's plea, writing, "I am literally in the same boat right now. Lots of my fellow actors are. I remember a time when we didn't have to earn a minimum to qualify for insurance. Glad to see that Jack has gotten an offer that will let them to qualify for 2027."

As detailed on the SAG Health Plan's eligibility page , the minimum threshold is expected to rise by approximately $900 each year until 2030. This year, members were required to earn $28,933. SAG-AFTRA did not respond immediately to comment.

Matarazzo's most recent project was the 2025 short film "Paper Tiger." She also starred "Welcome to the Dollhouse," "The Devil's Advocate" and "Scream 3," as well as multiple episodes of Netflix's "Wednesday."

articles.title: Gisele Bündchen Ended Her Marriage to Tom Brady With Just 3 Words
articles.summary: The former couple, who share two kids, divorced in 2022.
articles.body:
Tom Brady is the subject of an upcoming biography.

In Lars Anderson's Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness , a source close to the athlete claims that Gisele Bündchen was the one who ended their marriage.

Brady and Bündchen share two kids and were married for over a decade before divorcing in 2022.

A new book about Tom Brady reveals how his marriage to Gisele Bündchen crumbled. He and the supermodel were together for over a decade before divorcing in 2022.

In Lars Anderson's upcoming biography Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness , a source close to the athlete claims that Bündchen was the one who ended their relationship.

"One day, Gisele, who is really into astrology, basically looked into the stars and told Tom, 'We're not compatible,' and just like that, she was done," reads an excerpt published in the Daily Mail .

Anderson writes that Bündchen wanted Brady to retire from football as early as 2017, though his decision to continue playing put strain on their marriage.

According to Anderson, after Brady and the New England Patriots won the 2019 Super Bowl, Bündchen asked: "Would now be the perfect time to retire?"

"Too bad, babe. I'm having too much fun right now," Brady allegedly responded.

Anderson's book also claims that Bündchen wrote Brady a pointed message after the Patriots lost the 2018 Super Bowl.

"She needed him to be present when he was at home, not responding to text messages on his constantly buzzing cell phone or replaying a game in his mind," the author writes. "She needed more help with the kids. She needed the chance to sleep in just a few days a week. She needed more time for her own career."

A friend of Brady's explained how his career might have caused tension within his marriage.

"The guy gets up at the crack of dawn, thinks all day about a game that is foreign to his wife, comes home and is in bed each night by nine," the source said, according to Anderson. "He can't really eat out or go out without causing a scene. Everything he puts in his mouth tastes like shit. The whole lifestyle had to be getting tiresome for Gisele."

After playing with the Patriots for nearly two decades, Brady signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020, though he eventually retired in 2023.

Brady and Bündchen share two children—Vivian and Benjamin—while Brady also has a son named Jack from his relationship with Bridget Moynahan. Bündchen has since remarried, tying the knot with jiu-jitsu instructor Joaquim Valente in 2025. The couple welcomed their first child that same year.

articles.title: Oscar Piastri: I need a tow bar to hook onto Mercedes to fight for Baku win
articles.summary: Mercedes' pace in Baku means it's going to be difficult for anyone to compete with George Russell for the win
articles.body:
Having qualified third in Baku after enduring a difficult build-up to the main sessions, Oscar Piastri was happy with the grid position he earned for Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

However, the McLaren driver thinks expecting to go much further in the race is unrealistic, given the gap to Mercedes . While the Australian lost just 0.001s to Charles Leclerc in Q3, the deficit to George Russell was a massive 0.838s.

So when he was asked during the post-qualifying press conference whether he could challenge the Briton in the race, Piastri resorted to sarcasm.

"If he's got a tow bar that I can hook onto the back of, maybe," he smiled. "But yeah, we'll see what we can do."

Given the gap Russell managed to build over his rivals, it's easy to suggest his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli would have joined him on the front row had he not crashed in Q1 - and at a track where it's relatively easy to overtake, it's not entirely out of the question that Antonelli could still challenge Piastri in the race.

What's more, the McLarens didn't look particularly strong during the practice sessions, which could serve as a hint that the papaya cars may actually be on the defensive rather than the attack on race day. Piastri conceded that the weekend has been difficult for the Woking squad - but qualifying delivered a somewhat unexpected result.

Having not finished higher than sixth in any of the practice sessions, he was even briefly first during Q3, but that wasn't really a representative picture at a track which doesn't particularly suit this year's McLaren car.

On top of that, Piastri experienced a brake issue on Friday morning, forcing his team to use some unusual methods to combat the vibrations - tying some parts together with cable ties in order not to lose track time.

"It's been not an easy weekend, for sure, from a few areas," Piastri said. "You know, we've not been particularly quick. We were also running cable ties on our car through Friday, which is never a great sign. So it's been a little bit of a tricky one for us.

George Russell, Mercedes, Oscar Piastri, McLaren

"In qualifying we found a bit of pace. So, yeah, it's not the first time that's happened to us this year. We seem like we're a bit on the back foot through practice, we come out in qualifying and, yeah, we just find that bit extra.

"I was pretty surprised to see us 1-2 after the first lap of Q3, but unfortunately, we had no hope against George."

Still, the Australian reckons McLaren can fight the other teams on Saturday.

"The Mercedes look incredibly quick here," he said, "but everyone else looks like they're in a similar-ish kind of pack. And our race pace looked pretty good yesterday, to be honest. So I think we can hang on and battle in the pack behind George, and see what lap Kimi starts coming through as well."

Piastri's team-mate Lando Norris will line up fifth on the grid.

articles.title: Pabllo Vittar se move sob rastros de luz na foto da capa do álbum 'Lost in lust' | G1
articles.body:
Capa do álbum 'Lost in lust', de Pabllo Vittar — Foto: Hick Duarte com arte gráfica de Lucasphobia

♬ Pabllo Vittar se move sob rastros de luz na foto exposta na capa do sétimo álbum de estúdio da artista, “Lost in lust”. Programado para ser lançado na próxima quinta-feira, 1º de outubro, o álbum “Lost in lust” mostra Pabllo na capa em foto feita por Hick Duarte e enquadrada na arte gráfica criada por Lucasphobia.

Para chegar à imagem meio onírica da capa, a equipe de criação da artista optou por fotografar a cantora sob luz etérea e em clima sensual, para tentar traduzir na imagem o tom do álbum em que Pabllo Vittar ambienta 12 músicas – cantadas em inglês e/ou espanhol – em atmosfera eletrônica. Uma das referências visuais da capa foi a obra do fotógrafo italiano de moda Paolo Roversi.

Conceitualmente, o álbum “Lost in lust” – cujo título significa “Perdido na luxúria”, em bom português – é caracterizado como “uma jornada pelo desejo, pelo excesso, pela intimidade e pelo espaço indefinido entre o prazer e a obsessão”.

Ao longo das 12 faixas do álbum, a artista faz feat com o cantor venezuelano La Cruz em “Big bang”, se une ao astro italiano Mahmood em “Polizia”, divide o canto de “Body type” com Urias e traz a rapper porto-riquenha Villano Antillano em “Rockstar”.

“Alone”, “Attention”, “Bad good”, “Better than a feeling”, “Carnaval”, “Friend with...”, “Future” e “Skin” são as outras oito músicas que completam a tracklist do álbum “Lost in lust”.

articles.title: Cliente encontra pérola ao comer ostra em restaurante; VÍDEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Carina Lisboa encontrou a esfera ao provar um prato com ostra exótica em Cananéia. Restaurante participava de festival gastronômico voltado ao uso da espécie invasora.
articles.summary: Carina Lisboa encontrou a esfera ao provar um prato com ostra exótica em Cananéia. Restaurante participava de festival gastronômico voltado ao uso da espécie invasora.
articles.body:
Você já imaginou encontrar uma pérola ao comer uma ostra ? A situação parece roteiro de uma série de comédia, mas foi o que aconteceu com a personal trainer Carina Lisboa em Cananéia , no litoral de São Paulo ( assista acima ). Ao g1 , ela contou que só notou a pequena esfera que se assemelha a uma pérola quando já estava com ela na boca.

"Dei uma mordida e senti uma coisa dura. Eu falei: 'Nossa, acho que quebrei o meu dente, deve ter um pedaço de ostra aqui dentro'. Aí comecei a mexer e vi que tinha uma bolinha, que não tinha sido dente", relembrou a personal, de 41 anos.

O episódio ocorreu no restaurante Ponto das Ostras, no Centro da cidade. A proprietária do estabelecimento, Paula Monteiro, contou que foi a primeira vez que isso ocorreu com um cliente em 18 anos de comércio. "Meu pai trabalha com ostra desde os 13 anos e ele nunca tinha visto uma história dessa", explicou.

Pérola foi encontrada em um prato servido em um restaurante de Cananéia — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

O prato em que a esfera foi encontrada havia sido feito para o 1º Festival GastroMangue, promovido pela prefeitura com apoio da Universidade Estadual de São Paulo (Unesp) com o objetivo de desafiar restaurantes a criar receitas usando a ostra exótica Saccostrea cucullata.

Originária da Ásia, a ostra é considerada invasora porque tem se espalhado pela região, onde disputa espaço com espécies nativas. Dessa forma, o festival foi idealizado para transformar um problema ambiental em novas possibilidades gastronômicas e ajudar a discutir alternativas para o controle da espécie, extraída por pesquisadores da Unesp.

Ao g1 , Carina contou que estava fazendo uma caminhada com o aluno Jordinei Francisca no domingo (20) quando teve a ideia de almoçar no restaurante de Paula, amiga que havia lhe convidado para experimentar o novo prato envolvendo a ostra exótica.

A personal convidou o aluno para o almoço e, no estabelecimento, ainda encontrou a irmã e a cunhada. Todos estavam almoçando quando Carina sentiu a esfera na boca.

"Eu peguei a bolinha e falei: 'Gente, eu acho que achei uma pérola'. Aí todo mundo começou a rir na mesa", afirmou Carina, dizendo que todos duvidaram da raridade.

A personal chamou a proprietária do restaurante para mostrar a pequena esfera, que também ficou surpresa com o achado.

" Foi um daqueles momentos completamente inesperados, que a gente não planeja e que acabam virando uma história para contar . Para nós, foi uma experiência inusitada e inesquecível", explicou o cabeleireiro Jordinei, que gravou o vídeo mostrando a pérola.

Pérola foi encontrada durante almoço de Carina com o aluno Jordinei Francisca — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

Carina disse que entrou em contato com uma especialista em joias que confirmou se tratar de uma pérola ainda em formação. A personal trainer pretende transformá-la em um brinco de ponto de luz.

"Foi engraçado e foi um presente. Fiquei bem feliz porque eu sou muito da natureza, então eu creio que isso foi um presente de Deus para mim", explicou.

Os biólogos Alex Ribeiro e Ricardo Samelo explicaram que as pérolas são formadas por um mecanismo de defesa de moluscos bivalves, como ostras e mexilhões.

"O processo inicia quando um corpo estranho invade o corpo do animal. O sistema de defesa reconhece a partícula e tenta isolar a mesma criando um revestimento ao redor dela. Com o passar do tempo, mais material vai sendo adicionado, formando assim a pérola", afirmou Samelo.

De acordo com ele, o processo pode levar semanas, meses ou até anos. Os biólogos analisaram as imagens da esfera encontrada por Carina e acreditam que realmente se trata de uma pérola devido à assimetria dela.

"A pérola geralmente não é uniforme, como dá para a gente ver na imagem. Depois que os produtores pegam, ela é lapidada e passa por um processo para virar uma joia", disse Ribeiro.

Segundo o especialista, pérolas podem ser produzidas naturalmente, como provavelmente foi nesse caso, ou de forma artificial, em que produtores realmente inserem corpos nas ostras para estimular o mecanismo de defesa.

Ribeiro disse ainda que a cidade é conhecida pela produção de ostras por conta da qualidade da água e das condições ambientais da região. "As melhores ostras do estado de São Paulo são oriundas do litoral sul de Cananéia", afirmou.

articles.title: Caetano Veloso faz 'Coração vagabundo' bater de novo ao louvar João Gilberto em música do álbum de Cézar Mendes | G1
articles.body:
Capa do single 'João', de Cézar Mendes (à direita) com Caetano Veloso — Foto: Bob Wolfenson / Divulgação

♬ Conta o violonista e compositor baiano Cézar Mendes que, ao concluir o samba-canção “João” (2020), ele o mostrou ao muso inspirador da música, João Gilberto (10 de junho de 1931 – 6 de julho de 2019), e informou ao criador da bossa nova que a composição ganharia a voz de Caetano Veloso no álbum que Mendes planejava gravar.

Passaram-se anos entre a intenção e a realização, mas eis que “João” chegou ao mundo ontem, sexta-feira, 25 de setembro, como amostra inicial do segundo álbum de Cézar Mendes, o primeiro em que o artista se apresentará como intérprete, dando ele próprio voz a um cancioneiro autoral composto geralmente em parceria com Arnaldo Antunes, letrista de “João” e dos outras músicas do álbum previsto para ser lançado em novembro em edição da Uns Produções.

Só que, no caso de “João”, quem canta a música sozinho é mesmo Caetano Veloso em gravação que faz todo sentido dentro da trajetória do baiano tropicalista, devoto de João Gilberto desde 1958.

E tudo se afina não somente porque foi Caetano Veloso quem apresentou o conterrâneo santo-amarense Cézar Mendes ao Brasil como compositor – em 1998, 40 anos após a revolução de João – ao abrir parceria com o violonista na criação de “Aquele frevo axé”, samba cheio de bossa lançado na voz de Gal Costa (1945 – 2022) como música-título do álbum lançado pelo cantora naquele ano de 1998.

Quando Caetano canta os versos de “João”, louvando um dos mestres da música brasileira, é como se ele estivesse fazendo uma volta ao começo e fazendo bater novamente “Coração vagabundo”, a canção de 1967 que abriu o álbum dividido por Caetano com a mesma Gal Costa, então a Gracinha também devota de João. Tudo ali naquele dueto seminal era João e, por isso, tudo se encaixa agora em 2026.

A gravação de “João” por Caetano ecoa o dueto com Gal em 1967 inclusive por mostrar que, para ir na essência de uma canção – a lição maior deixada por João – nem sempre é preciso optar pela economia instrumental.

Diferentemente do que faz supor a foto de Bob Wolfenson na capa do single “João”, a gravação rejeita o formato minimalista de voz e violão. As cordas da St. Petersburg Studio Orchestra envolvem a gravação produzida e arranjada com esmero por Mario Adnet, também violonista da banda que inclui músicos como o ritmista Marcelo Costa (com bateria de toque reverente à leveza exigida por João Gilberto), o baixista Jorge Helder, o pianista Marcos Nimrichter e o flautista Eduardo Neves.

Parece muito, e é mesmo, mas tudo e todos estão em fina sintonia com João Gilberto.

Caetano Veloso (em pé) canta o samba-canção 'João' (2020) no segundo álbum do violonista Cézar Mendes, previsto para ser lançado em novembro — Foto: Bob Wolfenson / Divulgação

articles.title: Quote of the day by Sylvester Stallone: ‘We can’t succeed in everything. Most times, we lose. But the few times we do win, we have to make sure they were the important battles,’ a powerful life lesson explaining that winning the right fight matters more than winning all of them
articles.summary: Explore Sylvester Stallone's impactful quote on success, failure, and the importance of choosing the right battles in life. Discover how his journey from struggle to stardom encapsulates this message.
articles.body: Failure is something almost everyone experiences, but learning what is worth fighting for can change the way we look at it. Sylvester Stallone once spoke about this while reflecting on life, success and the legacy of his most famous character, Rocky Balboa. His words offer a simple idea: we may not win every battle, but the ones that truly matter deserve our effort.Today’s quote of the day by Sylvester Stallone reads: “I’m a big believer that, in life, we can’t succeed in everything. Most times, we lose. But the few times we do win, we have to make sure they were the important battles.”What does the quote by Sylvester Stallone mean?The actor expressed these thoughts in a 2006 interview with Total Film when explaining why he wanted Rocky to be remembered for the inspiration the character gave people. Stallone’s words seem to suggest that success does not have to be measured by winning every argument, competition or challenge. Some fights aren't worth wearing ourselves out over.Disappointments are in life. Plans go awry, opportunities are lost, and sometimes even our best efforts do not give us the result we hoped for. Stallone’s argument is that failure is not necessarily a failure in life. The key thing is knowing where to put our energy.The second part of his thought is especially important. If there are only a few moments when everything falls into place, those moments should involve things that genuinely matter to us. That could mean a career goal, a relationship, family, personal growth or a dream that we have refused to give up on.Why does his message still matter today?Modern life can make success look like a competition that never ends. One person is announcing a new job, another is celebrating an award, while someone else is sharing a new relationship, business achievement or personal milestone.Also, it is important to realise that not every setback needs to stay on our mind, and not every argument is worth spending our energy on. Sometimes, knowing what to leave behind can be just as important as knowing what to fight for. Sometimes, moving forward means knowing what to let go of and where to put your energy. Sometimes walking away from something is also a form of strength.His words also encourage people to think about priorities. Instead of trying to win everywhere, it may be more meaningful to protect the relationships, ambitions and values that matter most.Sylvester Stallone’s early lifeBorn on July 6, 1946, in New York City, Stallone did not enter Hollywood with an easy path to success. A medical complication at the time of his birth left Stallone with partial paralysis affecting some facial muscles. That condition became part of Stallone's distinctive screen presence, from the way he spoke to the expressions he made while acting.His journey in Hollywood was anything but smooth. Long before audiences knew him as an action star, Stallone took whatever small acting work he could find. Money was often tight, and finding steady work was not easy.With acting opportunities limited, he started putting more time into writing. It was a decision that eventually opened a completely different door for him. The story he wrote would go on to change the course of his career.Sylvester Stallone’s rise to fameEverything changed for Stallone when 'Rocky' arrived in 1976. He had written the screenplay and also played the lead, and the film quickly turned into a major success. It also earned him Academy Award nominations for his performance as well as his writing.Ultimately, “Rocky Balboa” was far more than a character in a boxing movie. His story touched people's hearts because it's about getting back up when things go wrong and continuing to believe in yourself. Stallone returned to the role over the years, with 'Rocky Balboa' bringing him back to the character in 2006.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: When Mushtaq Khan recalled Salman Khan's dating days, 'Welcome' actor said, 'Iss tarah ki baatein humne kabhi kari bhi nahi'
articles.summary: Mushtaq Khan passed away on Thursday evening at the age of 62. He had been battling cancer for a prolonged period.
articles.body: Mushtaq Khan passed away on Thursday evening at the age of 62. He had been battling cancer for a prolonged period. The veteran actor worked across several Hindi films and television shows during his career. His performance as Ballu in 'Welcome' remains among his best-known roles. The 2007 film was directed by Anees Bazmee. It featured Akshay Kumar, Katrina Kaif, Nana Patekar and Anil Kapoor in prominent roles.Mushtaq Khan had once shared an anecdote involving Salman Khan during the making of 'Welcome,' the movie that featured Katrina Kaif in the lead. The actor also spoke about questions surrounding Salman Khan's relationships.When Mushtaq Khan was asked about Salman Khan's dating daysIn an old interview with Filmymantra, Mushtaq Khan was asked about Salman Khan's dating life. He was specifically questioned about whether Sangeeta Bijlani had visited Salman Khan on a film set. The actor was also asked whether Salman Khan had visited Sangeeta Bijlani during shoots. Mushtaq Khan said such personal matters were not topics of discussion among them.He responded, "Iss tarah ki baatein humne kabhi kari bhi nahi aur kabhi poochha bhi nahi (We have never even discussed such things, nor have we ever asked about them).”Mushtaq Khan then recalled an occasion involving Salman Khan during the Dubai schedule of 'Welcome'. He said, “I have never seen Sangeeta ji come to the set to meet him, but once, when we were shooting the film 'Welcome' in Dubai, Salman came to the hotel there."Anupam Kher remembers Mushtaq KhanFollowing Mushtaq Khan's demise, several members of the film industry shared tributes. Anupam Kher posted a video remembering his professional association with the late actor.Anupam Kher recalled a period when the two actors worked together on several projects. He mentioned films associated with Mahesh Bhatt and Satish Kaushik.“There was a time when we worked together on a lot of films - Mahesh Bhatt's films, Satish Kaushik's films, and many others. Then we walked on our own paths. But I will always remember the days I spent with him."Anupam Kher also remembered Mushtaq Khan's personality and sense of humour. He added, "Mr Mushtaq was a very simple man. He had a great sense of humour. And I have never seen him angry."Suniel Shetty and Paresh Rawal pay tributeSuniel Shetty also expressed his grief after Mushtaq Khan's death. The actor remembered the veteran performer through a message on social media.Suniel Shetty wrote, "This one hurts. Some people leave behind memories that will always make you smile. My heartfelt condolences to the family. Rest in peace." Paresh Rawal also paid tribute to Mushtaq Khan. He remembered the late actor for his personality and his work as a performer.Paresh Rawal wrote, "Mushtaq Khan. Loving human being and an exciting actor. REST IN PEACE."Mushtaq Khan's career spanned films and television. articles.title: Dolly Parton's Young cancer survivor fan celebrates ‘9 to 5 Day’ at the hospital
articles.summary: Over the years, Dolly Parton invested in a lot of endeavours and believed in giving back to the community.
articles.body: Over the years, Dolly Parton invested in a lot of endeavours and believed in giving back to the community. Earlier this year, she donated a generous amount to a children’s hospital in Knoxville, which was renamed the Dolly Parton Children's Hospital in February 2026, only a few months before her passing.In a recent announcement, the children’s hospital revealed plans to hold a ‘9 to 5’ party to honour Dolly Parton’s commitment to charitable causes and her significant impact on countless individuals. At the centre of the celebration was 9-year-old Hattie Halter, a longtime fan of Parton and a patient at the hospital.Dolly Parton Children's Hospital to honour her legacy with a partyThe hospital revealed that they would hold a ‘9 to 5’ theme party to honour Parton’s legacy, and Halter, who was diagnosed with cancer when she was only nine months old, also attended the celebration. While talking to PEOPLE, her mother, Mellisa Halter, shared how her entire family will be there.She added, "I and her dad, her two brothers, and Hattie, we’re all going to be there bright and early. Being a part of anything that has to do with Dolly where she gets to talk to people about her, she’s just so excited.” She also recalled the time when her daughter had been diagnosed with leukemia and how harrowing the entire experience was for their family.She recalled, “It’s miserable and scary. You basically have to start treating the cancer as soon as possible so you really don’t have any time to process or think it through. It’s just a very scary thing to go from hoping they crawl and talk soon to, "Oh my gosh, is this going to kill my kid?" It’s something the little cute ‘how to prepare to be a mom’ books don’t necessarily warn you about.”Hattie Halter is a big fan of Dolly PartonHer mother also revealed that she has been a big fan of Parton and her music for years now, adding, “She loves her music, just her accent and the way she sings. And the fact that we have Dollywood here and she sees her everywhere in Tennessee, she just likes to dance and shimmy to her music.”Melissa further added, “I honestly feel like the way she carried herself—she exuded that kind of sunshine and happiness and wanting to help others—is what stuck out too, and Hattie just was attracted to that.”Days after the singer’s passing, the hospital shared a video of their patients and their parents sharing their experiences at the hospital and how they were able to overcome their diseases while remembering Parton. The caption under the post read, “Our patients and families express our feelings best. Dolly’s love and compassion will continue as we carry her light forward for generations to come. Thank you, Dolly.”About Dolly PartonThe country singer left for her heavenly abode on August 25 after a brief battle with cancer. The news of her passing was shared by her nephew, Bryan Seaver, in a video that was circulated on all of her social media accounts. The singer had been admitted to a cancer facility a few days before her passing. articles.body: Around a year ago, reports confirmed that Kris Jenner had decided to put the iconic ‘Keeping Up With The Kardashians’ mansion on the market. The online personality had been ready to part ways with the beloved house that appeared in most of the episodes of ‘Keeping Up With The Kardashians ’; however, new reports indicate Jenner is planning on holding on to the mansion for the time being.Kris Jenner pulls the ‘KUWTK’ house from the marketJenner has officially pulled the iconic mansion where most of the episodes of ‘KUWTK’ were filmed off the market. The news comes after the house had been up for sale for more than a year. ELLE Decor reported the news and shared that the mansion, which had earlier been listed for USD 13.5 million, has officially been put on hold, according to property records.Zillow reported that the house was first bought for USD 4 million in 2010 and has been under Jenner’s ownership for the past 16 years. Earlier this year, in May, the home had been briefly removed from the listing; however, she soon put it back up on the market for the same asking price. However, four months later, it has been confirmed yet again that the reality show house is no longer on the market.In another report shared by TMZ, Jenner may have had second thoughts about the home. Along with this, the home also features a massive chef’s kitchen covered in white, along with a large dining table and clear, cushioned chairs for the entire family.Last year, when she first listed the property on the market, the Jenner family matriarch revealed that she was ready for the house to move on to its next chapter. articles.summary: Heather Matarazzo, known for 'Princess Diaries,' reveals the risk of losing her SAG-AFTRA health insurance due to lack of work. Discover the challenges actors face within the industry and the rising income thresholds for health benefits.
articles.body: Heather Matarazzo recently revealed that she needs work or else she may soon lose her health insurance under SAG-AFTRA. The organisation requires actors to earn a minimum wage to qualify for health benefits. The 'Princess Diaries' star, who played Lilly Moscovitz in the film, revealed that she needs work to qualify.‘Princess Diaries’ star Heather Matarazzo says she may lose her health insurance without workIn a comment she posted recently, the ‘Princess Diaries’ star revealed that she is at risk of losing her health benefits. Earlier, Jack Haven, star of ‘Atypical’ and ‘I Saw The TV Glow,’ recently went viral for sharing their plight on social media, stating they needed work soon and needed USD 4000 to prevent their SAG-AFTRA health insurance under SAG-AFTRA from lapsing.While replying to an account that had shared the news about Haven’s plight, Heather admitted that she is going through the same thing. She posted, “I am literally in the same boat right now. Lots of my fellow actors are. I remember a time when we didn’t have to earn a minimum to qualify for insurance. Glad to see that Jack has gotten an offer that will let them qualify for 2027.”Heather last appeared in the 2025 film ‘Paper Tiger.' Other than that, she also had a recurring role in the OTT series 'Wednesday' alongside Jenna Ortega. She played the role of Judi Spannagel, the cheerful yet sinister executive assistant to Dr Rachael Fairburn at the Willow Hill Psychiatric Facility in season two of the hit show. Some of her other recent works also include ‘Welcome to the Dollhouse,' ‘The Devil’s Advocate,' and ‘Scream 3.' The actor, who recently appeared in ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,' shared, “I got a lot of offers. So, thank you, guys. Thank you for your love and your kindness. I really feel overwhelmed. articles.body: Horror film 'Evil Dead Burn' is set to premiere on HBO Max on October 2, giving fans of the franchise a chance to watch the latest instalment ahead of Halloween, Variety reported.One of the year's highly anticipated horror releases, "Evil Dead Burn" had its theatrical release on July 10 and marks the third film since the "Evil Dead" series reboot in 2013 and the sixth film overall in the franchise.Directed by Sebastien Vanicek, the film stars Souheila Yacoub, known for "Dune: Part Two", as a woman who seeks comfort from her in-laws following the death of her husband. However, their gathering at a secluded house soon turns into a terrifying reunion as the family members are transformed into Deadites.The film also stars Hunter Doohan, known for "Wednesday" and "Daredevil: Born Again", Luciane Buchanan of "The Night Agent", Tandi Wright of "Pearl", Erroll Shand of "Chief of War", George Pullar of "It Only Takes a Night" and Maude Davey of "The Newsreader".Created by Sam Raimi, the "Evil Dead" horror franchise now spans six films and a television series. The franchise follows various characters as they encounter demonic entities known as Deadites, which are raised with the help of a mysterious book of the dead, known as the Naturom Demonto in the first, fourth and fifth films, and as the Necronomicon Ex-Mortis in the second, third and sixth films, Variety reported.The original trilogy starred Bruce Campbell in "The Evil Dead" (1981), "Evil Dead II" (1987) and "Army of Darkness" (1992).The franchise continued with the 2013 standalone sequel "Evil Dead", followed by the Starz television series "Ash vs Evil Dead", in which Campbell reprised his role. The series ran from 2015 to 2018.The fifth film in the franchise, "Evil Dead Rise", was released in 2023. A seventh film, "Evil Dead Wrath", helmed by Francis Galluppi, is slated for an April 2028 release."Evil Dead Burn" has been produced by Raimi and Robert Tapert under their Ghost House Pictures banner. articles.body: Prince Harry gave a rare glimpse into how Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet are settling into school after their recent move back to the U.K. The Duke of Sussex spoke about his children on Friday, September 25, 2026, after completing a charity skydive in Ontario. Harry had promised 102-year-old World War II veteran Ed Marshall that he would take part in a jump, with the stunt also helping raise awareness and support for military charities.Once he was safely back on the ground, Harry was asked about life in Britain after returning with Meghan Markle and their two children. “It’s been great. He then joked that, after jumping out of a plane, it was also “great to be back on terra firma, actually!”How are Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet doing at their new school?According to Prince Harry, things are going well for the children. “The kids are happy in school, and it gives me a chance to really focus on Invictus in Birmingham,” he said, referring to the next Invictus Games, scheduled for July next year.The Duke and Duchess of Sussex, along with Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, arrived in England on August 26, 2026. Their spokesperson confirmed that the decision followed discussions with the family’s security team about the practicalities of their arrangements. They thanked the teachers for the care Archie and Lilibet had received.Reports at the time said the commute, including traffic and the repeated nature of the journey, had raised concerns for the family’s security team. Magazine.Prince Harry decided to turn the situation into a conversation instead of simply trying to get them out of the house. He told Archie and Lilibet about what he would be doing that evening and the children and families he would meet through his work with WellChild.“They were genuinely fascinated and asking all sorts of questions,” he said. The Duke added that he and Meghan try to use their work to help their children understand the world around them.The WellChild Awards celebrate children living with serious illnesses and the families and carers supporting them. Harry has been a patron of WellChild since 2007 and attended the 2026 ceremony for the 16th time, according to the charity.The event also gave Prince Harry another chance to talk about how becoming a parent has changed how he experiences the charity's work. He said meeting children and their parents now hits differently because he has Archie and Lilibet of his own.Prince Harry and Meghan Markle’s children are adjusting to life in the U.K.The school change is just one part of a much bigger adjustment for the Sussex family. Prince Harry and Meghan Markle had been living in California with Archie and Lilibet for several years before returning to Britain in August. articles.title: Karlos Arguiñano, chef: "Para hacer la tortilla de patatas perfecta no uses queso, usa 6 huevos, 3 patatas y 1 cebolla"
articles.standfirst: El reconocido cocinero desvela la fórmula definitiva para triunfar con la tortilla
articles.summary: El reconocido cocinero desvela la fórmula definitiva para triunfar con la tortilla
articles.body: La tortilla de patatas sigue desatando pasiones y debates acalorados en las cocinas españolas. Karlos Arguiñano, el cocinero más popular de la televisión, ha abordado en múltiples ocasiones este clásico gastronómico en su programa, dejando lecciones imborrables sobre su origen y preparación tradicional. A la hora de posicionarse sobre sus raíces históricas, el chef guipuzcoano lo tiene claro: "La tortilla de patatas, mientras no se demuestre lo contrario, se inventó en Navarra". En la eterna disputa sobre sus ingredientes básicos, el chef vasco no oculta su preferencia por la receta con cebolla, justificando que le aporta una jugosidad indispensable. Para Arguiñano, la diferencia entre opciones es rotunda: "La tortilla sin cebolla es campeona de Europa, pero con cebolla es campeona del mundo". Además, advierte contra los añadidos innecesarios que desvirtúan el plato tradicional, asegurando tajantemente que "la tortilla de patatas con cosas ya es otra cosa. Para la tortilla tradicional no uses queso. Con huevos, patatas, cebolla y sal tienes un manjar". Para lograr el equilibrio idóneo de ingredientes, propone una fórmula fija que nunca falla al cocinar en casa: "Para hacer la tortilla de patatas perfecta no uses queso, usa 6 huevos, 3 patatas y 1 cebolla". Respecto al punto exacto de cocción del huevo, el presentador huye de las posturas extremas y busca siempre la textura justa: "¿Cuajada o más crudita? Para mí, con cebolla siempre y en su punto". Uno de los momentos más delicados de la elaboración es el volteado. Para evitar accidentes trágicos en la cocina, recomienda pragmatismo e instrumentos adecuados: "Para darle la vuelta sin riesgos hay que usar una tapa o un plato llano más grande que la sartén. Nada de hacer malabares en el aire si no dominas la técnica, que se te cae al suelo y te quedas sin comida". Por último, el cocinero arremete contra las alternativas ultraprocesadas del supermercado, reivindicando el valor del trabajo artesanal: "Me gustan todas... menos las que venden envueltas en plástico. ¡Anda! No me digas que después de 6 años en la universidad y dos máster, te compras una tortilla envuelta en plástico. ¡Si tardas 25 minutos! El movimiento se demuestra andando y el cariño cocinando". Defendiendo siempre la cocina hecha en casa, concluye recordando que "la gente que no tiene cariño difícilmente va a hacer feliz a nadie".

articles.body: 'Hanuman Ansh' continues to stay in the box office conversation well into its second month, entering Day 51 with its India net collection now at Rs. 292.04 crore. Vishal Chaturvedi's spiritual biopic on Neem Karoli Baba, led by Shobhinaw Satyaa, has already crossed the Rs. 380 crore mark worldwide, an achievement few expected given its underwhelming start nearly two months ago. The film's ability to keep clocking numbers this far into its theatrical journey speaks to a devotion-driven audience base that has shown remarkable staying power.Hanuman Ansh Movie ReviewThe immediate domestic target for 'Hanuman Ansh' is the Rs. 300 crore India net milestone. At Rs. 292.04 crore, the film is Rs. 7.96 crore short of that mark on the current live tally. The next major benchmark on the worldwide front is Rs. 400 crore gross. Against the latest stated worldwide figure of Rs. 381.35 crore, that leaves a gap of Rs. 18.65 crore. Whether the film reaches either milestone will depend on its remaining theatrical run and the pace of collections in the coming days.'Hanuman Ansh's domestic box office run'Hanuman Ansh' had a slow start, collecting Rs. 1.08 crore in Week 1 and Rs. 0.40 crore in Week 2, before its trajectory changed in Week 3 with Rs. 10.40 crore. The film then entered a phase of extraordinary growth, adding Rs. 61 crore in Week 4, Rs. 90.25 crore in Week 5, Rs. 80.25 crore in Week 6 and a further Rs. 44.95 crore in Week 7, taking its cumulative net to Rs. 288.33 crore by the end of Day 49. The film added another Rs. 3.35 crore on Day 50 across 3,767 shows, pushing its India net to Rs. 291.53 crore and gross collection to Rs. 344.35 crore.‘Hanuman Ansh’ overseas collection and worldwide totalInternational collections have continued to add up steadily deep into the film's run. Having reached Rs. 36.50 crore in overseas gross by the end of Day 49, the film added another Rs. 0.50 crore on Day 50, taking its cumulative overseas total to Rs. 37 crore. Combined with its domestic numbers, this pushed the worldwide gross to Rs. 381.35 crore by the close of Day 50.'Hanuman Ansh' Day 51 collection live trackingAs per Sacnilk, 'Hanuman Ansh' is currently running across 2,411 shows on Day 51, having added Rs. 3.15 crore so far in the day.This takes the film's overall India gross to Rs. 348.07 crore and its India net to Rs. 294.68 crore, with the final Day 51 figure expected once all shows for the day have concluded.Day wise collections for 'Hanuman Ansh'Week 1: Rs. 1.08 croreWeek 2: Rs. 0.40 croreWeek 3: Rs. 10.40 croreWeek 4: Rs. 61.00 croreWeek 5: Rs. 90.25 croreWeek 6: Rs. 80.25 croreWeek 7: Rs. 44.95 croreDay 50: Rs. 3.35 croreDay 51 [LIVE]: Rs. 3.15 croreTOTAL: Rs. 294.68 croreMore about 'Hanuman Ansh'Directed and written by Vishal Chaturvedi, 'Hanuman Ansh' follows a young boy who, after suffering a devastating personal loss, embarks on a search for spiritual meaning rooted in themes of faith, compassion, humility and selfless service. articles.title: Chiranjeevi says Jason Sanjay ‘reminded me of his father Vijay during 1993-94’ at 'Sigma' event, backs his directorial debut and says ‘I wish Jason Sanjay also achieves his goals as a director’
articles.summary: Megastar Chiranjeevi’s praise for Jason Sanjay became one of the highlights of the Hyderabad pre-release event of 'Sigma'.
articles.body: Megastar Chiranjeevi’s praise for Jason Sanjay became one of the highlights of the Hyderabad pre-release event of 'Sigma'. Speaking as the chief guest, Chiranjeevi recalled his first meeting with the debutant filmmaker and said Jason’s appearance immediately reminded him of his father, actor-turned-politician Vijay, during his younger days.Chiranjeevi praises Jason Sanjay at 'Sigma' eventAs reported by Filmibeat, Chiranjeevi recalled meeting Jason for the first time and said his appearance took him back to the period when Vijay was still establishing himself in the film industry.“When he came to meet me, he reminded me of his father Vijay during 1993-94,” Chiranjeevi said.The veteran actor also revealed that he had asked Jason whether he wanted to pursue acting or direction. Jason, however, made his preference clear, telling Chiranjeevi that his real interest lay in writing and filmmaking.Chiranjeevi connects Jason Sanjay with Vijay’s family film legacyChiranjeevi also spoke about the filmmaking lineage Jason comes from. He pointed out that the young director has chosen a creative path closely connected to his grandparents, filmmaker S. A. Chandrasekhar and writer Shoba.“S S Chandrasekhar was a very good director, while his wife Shoba garu penned scripts. Sanjay is taking forward the skills of his grandparents. He has inherited those genes and has turned director,” he said.Chiranjeevi has previously worked with S. A. Chandrasekhar, giving him a long-standing association with Vijay’s family. His remarks therefore placed Jason’s debut within a film legacy spanning several generations, while also acknowledging the filmmaker’s decision to work behind the camera.Chiranjeevi recalls Vijay’s rise and wishes Jason success as a directorThe Megastar also recalled watching Vijay’s journey from his early years in cinema to becoming one of Tamil cinema’s leading stars. He said he hoped Jason would similarly find his own path and achieve his ambitions as a filmmaker.“I have seen his father Vijay rise to meteoric heights as an actor, and I wish Jason Sanjay also achieves his goals as a director. I think his debut film Sigma will pave the way for his dreams,” Chiranjeevi said.Jason Sanjay says Vijay is excited to watch 'Sigma' but will not promote itJason Sanjay has previously addressed his father Vijay’s involvement in the promotional campaign for Sigma. He said Vijay is looking forward to watching the film but will not actively promote it. Jason explained that Vijay’s responsibilities as Tamil Nadu Chief Minister were one reason for his absence from the promotional campaign. He also said he wanted the focus to remain on the film and its cast and crew rather than on his father’s presence.“My father is waiting for the release of Sigma. He won’t be promoting my film. I want the promotions to be about the film and not him. I don’t want it to overlap,” Jason said at a press interaction.At a recent 'Sigma' event, Jason Sanjay also acknowledged the support of his parents and sister, thanking his father Vijay, mother Sangeetha and sister Divya Saasha.'Sigma' marks Jason Sanjay’s first film as a director'Sigma', starring Sundeep Kishan and Faria Abdullah, is scheduled to release theatrically on October 2. Jason Sanjay is making his feature directorial debut with the film, which is produced by Lyca Productions.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.body: While Bollywood continues to dominate India’s film industry in terms of scale and commercial reach, Telugu cinema has steadily strengthened its presence, particularly with the rise of pan-India films. Nagarjuna follows in second place, while Amitabh Bachchan occupies the third position with an estimated net worth of Rs 4,000 crore.Chiranjeevi, Venkatesh Daggubati and Ram Charan also feature in top 10Three other major Telugu stars have also made it to the list. Megastar Chiranjeevi is ranked eighth with an estimated net worth of Rs 1,700 crore, while veteran actor Venkatesh Daggubati takes the ninth spot with an estimated wealth of Rs 1,650 crore.Ram Charan rounds off the top 10 with an estimated net worth of Rs 1,400 crore.India’s 10 richest actors in 2026, as per reported estimates1. articles.body: Nani and Srikanth Odela’s 'The Paradise' has entered Day 3 of its theatrical run, with the Nani-starrer witnessing continued audience activity on its first Saturday. The period action drama, which released worldwide on September 24, is playing in multiple languages and is heading into the crucial second half of its opening weekend.'The Paradise' Day 1 and Day 2 box office collections'The Paradise' opened its theatrical run with Rs 34.65 crore net in India on Day 1, according to Sacnilk-tracked figures. The film recorded 49.3% overall occupancy across 9,732 shows on its opening day. On Day 2, the Nani-starrer collected Rs 14.90 crore net in India, with overall occupancy reported at 32.8%. Internationally, the film added Rs. 3.00 crore gross on its second day, lifting its total overseas cumulative to Rs. 25.00 crore. With these overseas returns factored in, the movie's worldwide gross collection has now climbed to Rs. 97.50 crore.'The Paradise' Day 3 live trackingAs per Sacnilk, 'The Paradise' has collected Rs 4.81 crore net in India on Day 3 so far, with the Saturday figure continuing to change as additional shows report. The film is running across 3,478 shows and has recorded around 23.6% overall occupancy at the time of the update.The Telugu version is leading the Saturday business with Rs 4.23 crore live, followed by the Hindi version at Rs 46 lakh and Tamil at Rs 12 lakh.The Telugu version has recorded around 34% occupancy across 1,767 shows, while Hindi has registered approximately 12% occupancy across 1,446 shows. The Tamil version has recorded around 17% occupancy across 265 shows.Since Saturday collections are still being updated, the final Day 3 total could be higher once the remaining shows are added.'The Paradise' heads into crucial Sunday collectionsSaturday is an important day for 'The Paradise' as the film looks to build on its opening-day numbers and maintain momentum through the first weekend. The film had already recorded substantial advance interest before release, while its September 24 theatrical debut was supported by special-show arrangements and increased ticket prices in Telangana.Nani’s 'The Paradise': Cast, director and release detailsDirected by Srikanth Odela, The Paradise stars Nani in the lead role, with Raghav Juyal, Kayadu Lohar, Sonali Kulkarni and Mohan Babu among the principal cast members. articles.summary: Princess Diana’s brother reveals surprising details about her private life, including a powerful American suitor, royal tensions and plans for a fresh start.
articles.body: Princess Diana’s younger brother, Charles Spencer, released his memoir "Swan Song," about the beloved royal this week revealing new details about the late royal’s life behind palace walls. From claims about then-Prince Charles’ treatment of Diana to an American politician who reportedly courted her after her divorce, here are some of the memoir’s biggest revelations. Charles' reaction to Diana's death Spencer wrote that on the morning Diana died, then-Prince Charles sounded "giddily elated – like a lottery winner," he remembered thinking at the time. He wrote that Charles was "strangely matter-of-fact, given the enormity of the disaster." PRINCESS DIANA'S HONEYMOON LETTER REVEALS A YOUNG BRIDE 'PLAYING WITH GROWN-UPS' IN THE ROYAL FAMILY In hindsight, Spencer wrote, he believed that Charles’ first reaction to her death was that it likely freed him up to "marry the woman he loved, rather than appreciating the loss of one he did not." He also wrote that while they were arguing over funeral arrangements, Charles told him, "Rest assured … we'll forget her soon enough!" PRINCE HARRY'S RUMORED DIANA FILM 'MIGHT FEEL LIKE ANOTHER BETRAYAL' TO PRINCE WILLIAM AS RIFT GROWS: EXPERT Spencer said he was stunned for a few seconds before responding, "I can’t believe you just said that," before hanging up. Earlier in their conversation, Spencer wrote that Charles accused the Spencer family of having no sense of duty because Spener had objected to Princes Harry and William walking behind their mother’s coffin. PRINCESS DIANA NEVER FORGAVE SARAH FERGUSON FOR ONE BETRAYAL THAT ENDED THEIR FRIENDSHIP: BOOK Spencer wrote that he believed the diatribe was the result of Charles’ "pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death." After the excerpt from the book was released last week, Buckingham Palace issued a rare statement. "While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss," the statement said. Diana considered moving to South Africa with heart surgeon boyfriend Spencer wrote that after falling in love with heart surgeon Dr. Hasnat Khan following her divorce, Diana had the "naïve yet impossible" dream of moving to South Africa — where Spencer lived at the time — with her boyfriend because England had become "intolerable" to her. "Might they, she dared hope, move there together, and carve out a life?" he wrote. He said she dreamed that Khan could work at a hospital in Cape Town, and they could live "happily — normally — nearby" her brother. "The other side of the world seemed to offer the possibility of asylum," he wrote. INSIDE PRINCESS DIANA AND JFK JR.'S SECRET MEETING THAT FUELED ROMANCE RUMORS FOR DECADES One of Diana’s post-divorce suitors was an American politician Spencer said that Diana once asked him if he thought she’d make a good American first lady, explaining that one of her "many powerful aging American suitors, keen to secure her as the ultimate trophy wife, had told her he was sure to win the presidency if she married him." He said that Diana was more "titillated" by the idea of living in the White House than by the prospect of marrying the "would-be elderly husband." Diana, he said, had a "mischievous attraction to reinventing herself in a role that would make her enemies in the British Royal Family sick with jealousy, while ushering in an era of glamour in the White House that would surely have surpassed even that of the Jackie Kennedy years." Diana almost canceled the ‘Panorama’ interview Despite "Panorama" reporter Martin Bashir allegedly telling Diana a series of falsehoods, including that she was being surveilled by MI6, that Prince William was unwittingly bugging her through a device on his watch and that her children’s nanny had aborted Prince Charles' child after an affair, Diana almost canceled the interview, Spencer said. But Bashir and the show’s executive producer persisted, Spencer wrote. He said they arranged a clandestine meeting in a parking garage, where Spencer believes they persuaded Diana that her life was in "imminent" danger and that doing the interview was the best way to protect herself. Spencer depicts then-Prince Charles as resentful of his position Spencer said he had a conversation with Charles after his own father’s funeral, during which Charles told him he was "lucky" his father had died because he got to inherit when he was "so young." articles.title: In 2014, Akon launched a solar initiative to bring electricity to rural Africa; within a year, it reached 14 countries
articles.summary: Long before solar energy became a major part of conversations around Africa’s development, Akon was trying to tackle one of the continent’s most basic
articles.body: Long before solar energy became a major part of conversations around Africa’s development, Akon was trying to tackle one of the continent’s most basic challenges: access to electricity.In February 2014, the Senegalese-American singer launched Akon Lighting Africa, an initiative focused on using solar power to provide electricity to communities that were not connected to reliable power networks. The project was founded by Akon along with Thione Niang and Malian entrepreneur Samba Bathily.The idea was ambitious from the beginning. The initiative initially set out to bring electricity to one million African households by the end of 2014, with a particular focus on rural communities. Its approach involved solar equipment for homes as well as public infrastructure, rather than relying solely on conventional electricity grids.Why Akon wanted to focus on electricityFor Akon, the project was connected to his own childhood experience in Senegal. He and co-founder Thione Niang grew up in Kaolack, a town where access to electricity was limited. The initiative’s official account says those experiences of growing up without reliable power helped shape their decision to make energy access a priority. The reasoning behind the project went beyond simply putting lights in homes. Lack of electricity affects education, healthcare and economic activity.Solar power became the answerInstead of waiting for conventional electricity infrastructure to reach remote communities, Akon Lighting Africa promoted off-grid solar solutions.The programme worked through partnerships involving governments, businesses and organisations connected to the project. Its solutions included solar streetlights, household solar kits, community systems and solar-powered equipment.The model was also designed around financing. A 2015 statement from the initiative said solar systems were pre-financed so that equipment could be deployed more quickly, while governments and other partners participated in the wider process.From a 2014 launch to 14 countriesBy August 2014, only months after the initiative was launched, a report from Northwestern University’s Medill News Service said Akon had stated that solar installations had already reached 14 African nations. At that point, the project had completed about a quarter of its stated one-million-household target, according to the report.The initiative’s own subsequent overview similarly says that in less than one year, solar solutions including streetlights and domestic and individual kits had been installed in 14 African countries.Those countries included Mali, Senegal, Niger, Guinea, Burkina Faso, Sierra Leone, Benin, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, the Republic of Congo, Namibia, Madagascar, Kenya and Nigeria.The rapid expansion was not limited to individual houses. According to the initiative, projects reached villages, community buildings, schools and health centres, with some rural communities receiving electricity for the first time.More than streetlightsThe programme was built around the idea that electricity could change how communities function after sunset.Solar streetlights could illuminate roads and public spaces, while household systems could provide lighting and allow residents to charge phones and use basic electrical devices. The initiative also highlighted employment opportunities created through the installation and maintenance of solar equipment, particularly for young people.The project’s focus later expanded to training as well. Akon Lighting Africa and its partners developed the Solektra Solar Academy in Bamako, Mali, aimed at training young Africans in solar technology, including installation and maintenance.The bigger ambitionReaching 14 countries was presented as an early stage rather than the end goal.A 2015 United Nations Sustainable Energy for All forum document said the initiative had already reached 11 countries at that point and was seeking to accelerate rural electrification threw off-grid solar solutions.The project’s longer-term plans were considerably larger. Its stated ambition was to expand across more African countries and address energy access on a continental scale. Later project material lists 25 countries where it had projects or planned phases.The initiative also attracted attention from international organisations. In May 2015, its founders were invited to the United Nations and World Bank-backed Sustainable Energy for All Forum, where the project was presented as an example of a market-based approach to expanding energy access.Akon’s project therefore became notable not simply because a major music star entered the energy sector, but because of how quickly the initiative attempted to move from an announced goal to physical solar installations across multiple African countries. Launched in February 2014 with a target of bringing electricity to one million households, Akon Lighting Africa had reached 14 countries in less than a year, according to the project’s own account and contemporary reporting. Its work combined solar technology, public-private partnerships and local employment with a much larger objective: finding practical alternatives for communities that conventional electricity infrastructure had not yet reached.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
